items.detail: holder_store.go:26 sets a three minute TTL on the holder record while the exclusion record has none, because holder_scripts.go:675 expire_keys is called only at 968 and 1094 in the holder record scripts and never in the exclusion scripts. A heartbeat gap longer than the TTL removes the holder record without changing BootID, and the registration script at 911 falls through to the unconditional HSET at 956 when the record is absent, so the same boot re-registers and load_placement at 1144 resumes returning the real excluded state with an owner that no longer exists. The record is then neither releasable nor re-excludable. NOT_FOUND now keeps the plan BLOCKED with backoff retry; only BOOT_MISMATCH is inert because only it positively proves a new generation took over
items.liveness_argument: under StatefulSet semantics the Pod always returns; same boot moves capture to OK and takes the normal CAS release, a new boot moves it to BOOT_MISMATCH. step 4 now requires resourceVersion not equal to V0, unchanged UID, and spec.replicas equal to expected, with any failure treated as unknown or as adopted committed. If a patch type does not enforce the resourceVersion precondition, an in-flight UpdateScale can commit first and the barrier patch can still return a different RV, which would previously have been declared NOT_COMMITTED and would have let section 8.3 release the exclusion into a Pod being deleted
items.rule_derived: SP-BAR-3 makes the two extra comparisons unconditional and explicitly not waivable by any passing gate, because the response body already contains the full object and a cheap fallback beats a precise assumption

items.detail: the barrier operation is closed by an exact GET comparing the annotation nonce with the nonce persisted in the operation record; equal means committed, unequal with RV equal to V0 means not committed and a new nonce is used, and only a failed read is unknown. This terminates because the barrier effect is idempotent and observable, so no further write is needed. Any implementation that resolves a barrier operation by issuing another write is a section 17 stop condition, since the active set would never empty and EXCLUSIVE would livelock

the discriminator is no longer whether the writer holds a lease but whether it can prove it is looking at current state. Channel A is a valid mutation lease; channel B is a one-time audit capability binding detector identity, the store_epoch pinned at the start of the AuditPage run and an evidence digest, CAS'd on that epoch. A stale-fence controller fails both because its epoch is behind. The section 6.10 negative case subject is narrowed from any lease-less writer to a stale fence controller, and a positive case plus an epoch-drift negative case are added

items.detail: the header said any missing check means unknown while the three branches assigned three different non-unknown outcomes, so neither could be followed. The header now says classify by the table and fixes the evaluation order as (b) then (a) then (c). Branch (c) was a two-way split on spec.replicas but the threat model has three value classes, so a third-party value modelled by F43 was being classified as adopted committed, which routes to the section 8.3 COMMITTED row and leaves a live same-boot victim with a permanently unreleasable exclusion. It is now a three-way split with the third value going to unknown

F58c is the one branch added to prove termination and its third case handed control to step 5 for the scale operation without saying what happens to the barrier operation, leaving it in the active set forever. It is now a four-row table where every row disposes of both operations, with the third row closing the barrier as SUPERSEDED because the safety property depends only on RV differing from V0 and not on who advanced it. The claim of necessary termination was replaced by an explicit decreasing measure, namely that the active set contracts monotonically because no branch emits a write, and sustained GET failure now escalates to a non-terminal operator-visible degraded state rather than being asserted away

the clearing procedure required proof that the detector held a valid fence at detection time, which a channel B detector never holds by construction, so a channel B latch could never be cleared and the realm was permanently locked. Clearing now forks on detector_identity: channel A proves a fence, channel B proves the capability was issued, unrevoked and bound to the same store_epoch as store_epoch_at_detection, which is the equivalent strength proof of having observed current state. The capability now has a named issuer tied to the coordinator trust root, a TTL, one-time consumption, revocation and rate limiting
items.equivalence_claim_corrected: a pinned store_epoch equals a mutation lease only on the staleness dimension; on the concurrency dimension it is strictly weaker because two concurrent same-epoch detectors are not mutually excluded, which is harmless for a latch but does not exclude a buggy concurrent detector
items.dos_surface: acknowledged as intended rather than defended away: any holder of a valid audit capability can permanently fail-close a realm, because that is precisely the value of a latch. Mitigation lives in issuance, revocation and rate limiting, not in weakening the ability to set it

items.detail: StatefulSet semantics guarantee the Pod object is recreated, not that the Holder process registers, and only registration creates the record current_holder reads. CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, unschedulable, unbound PVC and a NotReady node all leave the Pod indefinitely unregistered, and the section 14.1 requirement to apply a ResourceQuota and a low priority PriorityClass makes an indefinitely Pending Pod more likely rather than less
items.harm_decomposition: the exclusion record itself is harmless while NOT_FOUND persists, because with no holder record current_holder rejects before load_placement is reached and nothing can be placed on that holderID anyway. items.justification: DEGRADED feeds no safety decision. Every DEGRADED path leaves the plan BLOCKED, which is already fail-closed, so a count lost to a restart buys extra retries rather than an unsafe action. Shapes (a) and (b) both require editing model.go or state_machine.go, which are A1-forbidden, and (b) would add a second BlockedReason mutation path to a state machine whose whole design is that the reason is fixed once determined
items.accepted_cost: after a controller restart the operator-visible DEGRADED signal resets, so a plan that keeps failing across restarts may never surface it. This is a monitoring gap, not a correctness one, and it is the reason the decision is recorded rather than assumed

items.problem: the one-time audit capability needs an issued-and-unrevoked set, but the frozen keyspace has no key for it, no contract owns it, no retention or cap is defined, and the script checks only revocation. Checking revocation alone accepts capabilities that were never issued. The frozen ACL in 6.12 also has no read-only auditor principal, while channel B's premise is a read-only auditor performing one write
items.owner_stage: A1 for keyspace and script, A0.5 for the 6.12 ACL principal
items.default_rationale: one usable channel beats claiming two
items.if_skipped: the only fail-open-flavoured item on the list. Operators would expect an auditor to be able to block writes when in fact it cannot
items.decision: delete channel B rather than complete it. Executed in the document, not merely recorded
items.justification: the gap is real but currently inert. There is no auditor role in the system, AuditPage has no caller, and the ACL has no read-only audit principal. A gap on a path nobody walks carries no live risk
items.correction_to_first_draft: the first draft justified this as removing redundancy nobody asked for. That was wrong in the place it mattered. Channel B is not redundant: per-operation validation has a bounded scope and never scans the realm, AuditPage exists precisely to cover the depth it cannot see, so channel B was the only path by which deep corruption could stop further writes
items.accepted_cost: corruption found by AuditPage outside the touched-key set can only produce a read-only report. It cannot latch, and later mutations will not rediscover it because their validation scope is bounded. A realm known to be corrupt keeps being written to until a human reads the report
items.cost_of_building_it_instead: a coordinator-issued short-lived capability plus issuance, revocation and rate-limiting; a Lua-side CAS against the issued-and-not-revoked set, since checking only revocation accepts credentials that were never issued; and a separate appeal path for clearing a mis-set latch. Section 6.5 has no key for it and section 11.2 has no contract owning it
items.reopen_trigger: AuditPage acquires its first real runner. Before that the gap is inert; after it, the gap is fail-open
